newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul approves $65 mln arena interim bond plan.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul approves $65 mln arena interim bond plan.

text.p: St. Paul on Monday agreed to guarantee $65 million interim financing for a new arena if the National Hockey League awards an expansion team to the city, Mayor Norm Coleman's spokesman said.

Already committed to provide $30 million for a new downtown arena, the St. Paul City Council voted 6-1 to provide another $65 million if promised state financing fails to materialize next year, spokesman Paul Adelmann said.

Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson has been a strong supporter of the bid for a new NHL expansion franchise and has pledged to include $65 million of bonds for the arena project in the capital projects budget next year.
The interim financing plan would use four revenue streams to support debt service on $65 million of general obligation bonds for the estimated $130 million arena, mayoral aides have said.
Those sources of revenue include marquee advertising, an existing sales tax, a hotel/motel tax and an existing tax increment financing district.
The NHL has chosen investor groups in St. Paul, Atlanta, Columbus, Ohio, Houston, Nashville and Oklahoma City as finalists for future expansion.

"We feel very good that our city has done its job and put together what we need to put together," Adelmann said. "We still hope we will get state bonding in the next session to cover the $65 million portion of the financing."
The league has not announced a schedule for expansion or stated how many franchises it will award. The NHL expansion committee meets next on Wednesday.
